# Bufferbloat harness: HTB + `fq_codel` vs `pfifo_fast` over a veth pair

A single self-contained Bash script that builds a two-namespace veth testbed,
shapes it to 8 Mbit with a 20 ms base RTT, runs three concurrent TCP flows, and
machine-checks:

* per-flow throughput within 10 % of a fair share,
* 95th-percentile standing queue below 10 ms while the link is ≥ 80 % utilized,
* per-flow throughput, RTT percentiles, drops and ECN marks, and max qdisc
  backlog in a JSON report,
* the same tree with a `pfifo_fast` leaf as a contrast run that must
  *demonstrate* bufferbloat (otherwise the harness exits non-zero too).

It exits non-zero when any target is missed.

---

## 1. Root-cause analysis

### 1.1 Why a deep FIFO produces bufferbloat

`pfifo_fast` is the kernel's default qdisc and is little more than a 3-band
tail-drop FIFO. Its depth is the interface `txqueuelen` (1000 packets by
default). A TCP sender keeps increasing its congestion window until it sees
loss. With a 1000-packet tail-drop buffer and an 8 Mbit bottleneck:

```
1000 packets x 1500 B = 1.5 MB
1.5 MB x 8 / 8_000_000 = 1.5 s of queuing delay
```

All flows of the same DSCP land in the same band, so there is no per-flow
isolation and no AQM. The queue becomes a *standing* queue: while the link is
saturated it never drains, so the *local minimum* RTT (the quantity CoDel
controls) stays elevated for as long as the load lasts. This is bufferbloat.

### 1.2 Why an HTB class with an `fq_codel` leaf fixes it

* **HTB** is a classful token-bucket shaper. It is what actually imposes the
  8 Mbit bottleneck and gives us a class tree to attach the AQM to.
* **`fq_codel`** = fair queuing + CoDel. It hashes each packet's flow
  (`skb_get_hash`, i.e. the 5-tuple plus a per-qdisc random perturbation) into
  one of `flows` per-flow queues, serves those queues round-robin using
  `quantum` bytes of deficit (DRR), and runs an independent CoDel instance on
  each. Three bulk TCP flows therefore each receive ≈ 1/3 of the shaped rate
  *and* each gets its own delay control loop.
* **CoDel** tracks packet *sojourn time* (not queue length). It tolerates
  bursts but keeps the local minimum sojourn near `target` (5 ms). Once the
  minimum exceeds `target` for more than `interval`, it drops/marks to force
  the senders down. Because the control variable is time in the queue, the
  steady-state queue is bounded in milliseconds regardless of the link rate.
* **ECN**: `fq_codel` has `ecn` **on by default** (the `tc-fq_codel(8)` man
  page says so explicitly, unlike `codel`). When both endpoints negotiate
  ECN, CoDel sets CE instead of dropping, so `tc -s qdisc` reports
  `ecn_mark > 0` and drops near zero.

### 1.3 The `tc` stacking trap (why `netem` is on the return path)

`netem` is a **classless, terminal** qdisc:

* it cannot be the parent of an `fq_codel` leaf, and
* a class can have exactly one child qdisc, so you cannot hang both `netem`
  and `fq_codel` off the same HTB class.

The usual "apply `netem delay` and `htb`/`fq_codel` on the same interface root"
recipe is therefore impossible without an extra device. The harness avoids it
by putting:

* the **bottleneck + AQM** on the *forward* path
  (`root 1: htb -> 1:1 -> 1:10 -> 10: fq_codel`), and
* the **20 ms propagation delay** on the *return* path
  (`root 1: netem delay 20ms` on the peer).

TCP's RTT is a round trip, so 20 ms of one-way delay on the ACK path produces a
20 ms base RTT while leaving the forward path free for the real qdisc under
test. (If you ever need delay *and* shaping in the same direction, redirect to
an IFB device and shape the IFB's egress — noted as an extension in §5.)

### 1.4 The measurement trap (sparse flows vs the standing queue)

A `ping`/ICMP flow hashes into a **different** `fq_codel` bucket and is served
as a sparse ("new") flow, so its RTT stays near the base even while the bulk
flows have a queue. Measuring only ping RTT therefore *understates* the
standing queue. The harness measures the standing queue two independent ways
and takes the conservative maximum:

1. **Backlog-derived queue delay** — sample `tc -s qdisc` at 10 Hz and convert
   backlog bytes to time:
   `delay_ms = backlog_bytes * 8 / rate_bps * 1000`.
   Report `max qdisc backlog` in bytes and packets.
2. **RTT inflation** — `p95(loaded ping RTT) - p50(idle ping RTT)`.

This is faithful to CoDel's own definition: it controls *packet-sojourn time*,
which for a saturated link is the standing queue.

### 1.5 Why the `pfifo_fast` contrast is a target, not an afterthought

The contrast run uses the *same* HTB tree and the *same* 8 Mbit rate, but a
`pfifo_fast` leaf. If its p95 standing queue is not dramatically worse than
`fq_codel`'s, the experiment failed to demonstrate anything (e.g. the load was
too small or the qdisc was not applied), so the harness treats that as a
failed target and exits non-zero. The pass condition is
`pfifo_p95 >= max(20 ms, 2 x fq_codel_p95)`.

---

## 2. Topology

```
   bl_cli namespace                         bl_srv namespace
  +--------------------+                  +--------------------+
  |  vc <ip-address>/24   |<=== veth pair ===>|  vs <ip-address>/24   |
  |                    |                  |                    |
  | egress = BOTTLENECK|  forward data -> |                    |
  | root 1: htb 8mbit  |                  | egress = netem     |
  |   1:1              |  <- ACKs (delay) | root 1: netem      |
  |    1:10            |                  |      delay 20ms    |
  |     10: fq_codel   |                  |                    |
  +--------------------+                  +--------------------+
      iperf3 -c (x3)                         iperf3 -s (x3)
      ping under load                        (ACK path)
```

Direction under test is client → server ("upload"), so the bottleneck is the
client egress qdisc. Three one-shot `iperf3 -s -1 -p 5201..5203` servers and
three concurrent `iperf3 -c` clients produce three independent TCP flows.

---

## 3. Exact `tc` commands

These are the commands the harness issues (it also logs every command it runs
to `$WORKDIR/tc_commands.txt`, so the report is reproducible).

**Forward path — client egress `vc`: 8 Mbit bottleneck + `fq_codel` AQM**

```bash
tc qdisc add dev vc root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev vc parent 1:   classid 1:1  htb rate 8mbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
tc class add dev vc parent 1:1  classid 1:10 htb rate 8mbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
tc qdisc add dev vc parent 1:10 handle 10: fq_codel \
    limit 10240 flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5ms interval 100ms \
    ecn memory_limit 32mb drop_batch 64
```

**Return path — server egress `vs`: 20 ms base RTT**

```bash
tc qdisc add dev vs root handle 1: netem delay 20ms limit 10000
```

**Contrast run — same tree, FIFO leaf**

```bash
tc qdisc del dev vc root
tc qdisc add dev vc root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev vc parent 1:   classid 1:1  htb rate 8mbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
tc class add dev vc parent 1:1  classid 1:10 htb rate 8mbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
tc qdisc add dev vc parent 1:10 handle 10: pfifo_fast
```

**Inspection (what the analyser parses)**

```bash
tc -s -d qdisc show dev vc     # leaf backlog, dropped, ecn_mark
tc -s   class show dev vc      # per-class backlog fallback
```

`tc` parameter notes:

* `target 5ms` / `interval 100ms` are the CoDel defaults and are appropriate
  here: `interval` should be on the order of the worst-case RTT (20 ms base,
  100 ms is comfortably larger). RFC 8289 (CoDel) / RFC 8290 (`fq_codel`).
* `quantum 1514` = Ethernet MTU (1500) + L2 header (14). Correct for a
  veth/MTU-1500 path; change it if the MTU changes.
* `flows 1024` can only be set when the qdisc is created (the hash table is
  allocated at load time).
* `ecn` is already the default; it is written explicitly so the intent is
  unambiguous and so the report's `ecn_mark` counter is expected.

---

## 4. The harness (drop-in script)

Save as `bufferbloat_harness.sh`, `chmod +x`, run as root with `iperf3`
installed. It creates and tears down its own namespaces; nothing on the host
interface is touched.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# bufferbloat_harness.sh
#
# Reproducible bufferbloat / fairness harness built on a veth pair in private
# network namespaces.
#
#   client ns (bl_cli) --- vc ======= vs --- server ns (bl_srv)
#
# Direction under test is client -> server (upload), so the bottleneck qdisc is
# the *egress* qdisc of "vc" in the client namespace:
#
#     root 1: htb  (rate 8 Mbit)
#       +-- 1:1   (aggregate class)
#            +-- 1:10  (service class)
#                 +-- 10: fq_codel   (AQM leaf, ECN enabled)
#              or 10: pfifo_fast     (contrast leaf)
#
# A 20 ms base RTT is created with netem on the *return* path (server egress).
# TCP's RTT is a round trip, so 20 ms of one-way delay on the ACK path yields a
# 20 ms base RTT while leaving the forward path free for the real bottleneck
# qdisc (a qdisc cannot have both netem and HTB/fq_codel stacked in one
# direction without an extra IFB device).
#
# Two runs are executed:
#   fq_codel   - must meet: utilization, flow fairness, p95 standing queue
#   pfifo_fast - contrast; must demonstrate bufferbloat (p95 queue >> target)
#
# A machine-checkable JSON report is written to $REPORT.
# Exit status is 0 only if the fq_codel run passes every target *and* the
# pfifo_fast contrast run demonstrates the expected bufferbloat.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ------------------------------- configuration ------------------------------
NS_S="${NS_S:-bl_srv}"                 # server namespace (ACK sender)
NS_C="${NS_C:-bl_cli}"                 # client namespace (bottleneck egress)
VS="${VS:-vs}"                         # veth end inside server ns
VC="${VC:-vc}"                         # veth end inside client ns (bottleneck)
IP_S="${IP_S:-<ip-address>}"
IP_C="${IP_C:-<ip-address>}"
PREFIX="${PREFIX:-24}"

RATE_STR="${RATE_STR:-8mbit}"          # HTB shaping rate
LINK_RATE_BPS="${LINK_RATE_BPS:-8000000}"
BASE_RTT_MS="${BASE_RTT_MS:-20}"       # netem one-way delay on return path
NUM_FLOWS="${NUM_FLOWS:-3}"
DURATION="${DURATION:-30}"
SAMPLE_INTERVAL="${SAMPLE_INTERVAL:-0.1}"
PORT_BASE="${PORT_BASE:-5201}"

TARGET_UTIL="${TARGET_UTIL:-0.80}"              # >= 80% link utilization
TARGET_FAIRNESS="${TARGET_FAIRNESS:-0.10}"      # each flow within +/-10%
TARGET_QUEUE_P95_MS="${TARGET_QUEUE_P95_MS:-10}" # p95 standing queue < 10 ms
CONTRAST_MIN_MS="${CONTRAST_MIN_MS:-20}"        # pfifo_fast p95 must exceed
CONTRAST_RATIO="${CONTRAST_RATIO:-2.0}"         # ... and beat fq_codel by 2x

LEAF_HANDLE=10
MIN_IPERF_MIN="${MIN_IPERF_MIN:-10}"   # sanity: iperf duration must be >= this

WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(mktemp -d /tmp/bufferbloat.XXXXXX)}"
KEEP_WORKDIR="${KEEP_WORKDIR:-0}"
SKIP_PRIVCHECK="${SKIP_PRIVCHECK:-0}"
REPORT="${REPORT:-$WORKDIR/report.json}"
TC_LOG="$WORKDIR/tc_commands.txt"
RUNNING="$WORKDIR/.running"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"

log()  { printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date +%H:%M:%S)" "$*" >&2; }
die()  { log "ERROR: $*"; exit 1; }

SRV_PIDS=()
CLI_PIDS=()
BG_PIDS=()

# shellcheck disable=SC2329  # invoked indirectly via trap
cleanup() {
  local rc=$?
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
  rm -f "$RUNNING" 2>/dev/null || true
  local p
  for p in "${BG_PIDS[@]:-}" "${CLI_PIDS[@]:-}" "${SRV_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$p" ] && kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  wait 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns del "$NS_S" 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns del "$NS_C" 2>/dev/null || true
  [ "$KEEP_WORKDIR" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$WORKDIR"
  exit "$rc"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

# ----------------------------------- checks ----------------------------------
[ "$SKIP_PRIVCHECK" = 1 ] || [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] \
  || die "must run as root (or set SKIP_PRIVCHECK=1 for the mock test harness)"
for c in ip tc iperf3 ping python3; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required tool not found: $c"
done
[ "$DURATION" -ge "$MIN_IPERF_MIN" ] \
  || die "DURATION=$DURATION is too short for stable statistics (>= $MIN_IPERF_MIN)"

if command -v modprobe >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for m in sch_htb sch_netem sch_fq_codel cls_u32; do
    modprobe "$m" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
fi

# ------------------------------- tc helpers ----------------------------------
tc_s() { printf 'tc %s\n' "$*" >>"$TC_LOG"; ip netns exec "$NS_S" tc "$@"; }
tc_c() { printf 'tc %s\n' "$*" >>"$TC_LOG"; ip netns exec "$NS_C" tc "$@"; }

# ---------------------------------- topology ---------------------------------
setup_topo() {
  ip netns del "$NS_S" 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns del "$NS_C" 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns add "$NS_S"
  ip netns add "$NS_C"
  ip link add "$VS" type veth peer name "$VC"
  ip link set "$VS" netns "$NS_S"
  ip link set "$VC" netns "$NS_C"
  ip netns exec "$NS_S" ip addr add "$IP_S/$PREFIX" dev "$VS"
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" ip addr add "$IP_C/$PREFIX" dev "$VC"
  ip netns exec "$NS_S" ip link set lo up
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" ip link set lo up
  ip netns exec "$NS_S" ip link set "$VS" up
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" ip link set "$VC" up
  # pfifo_fast's depth is the interface txqueuelen; keep the classic 1000.
  ip netns exec "$NS_S" ip link set "$VS" txqueuelen 1000
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" ip link set "$VC" txqueuelen 1000
  # ECN is required for fq_codel to mark instead of drop.
  ip netns exec "$NS_S" sysctl -qw net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=1 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" sysctl -qw net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=1 2>/dev/null || true
}

# 20 ms base RTT: delay the return path only.
apply_netem() {
  tc_s qdisc del dev "$VS" root 2>/dev/null || true
  tc_s qdisc add dev "$VS" root handle 1: netem delay "${BASE_RTT_MS}ms" limit 10000
}

# HTB class tree + fq_codel AQM leaf.
#
# fq_codel grew parameters over time.  Try the modern full set first and fall
# back so the harness also runs on older kernels:
#   limit/flows/target/interval/quantum/ecn : Linux >= 3.5 (original fq_codel)
#   ce_threshold / ce_threshold_*           : Linux >= 4.2 / >= 5.16 (unused)
#   memory_limit                            : Linux >= 4.7
#   drop_batch                              : Linux >= 4.7
# (See the kernel-version notes in the accompanying write-up.)
apply_fq_codel() {
  tc_c qdisc del dev "$VC" root 2>/dev/null || true
  tc_c qdisc add dev "$VC" root handle 1: htb default "$LEAF_HANDLE"
  tc_c class add dev "$VC" parent 1: classid 1:1 htb \
      rate "$RATE_STR" ceil "$RATE_STR" quantum 1514
  tc_c class add dev "$VC" parent 1:1 classid "1:$LEAF_HANDLE" htb \
      rate "$RATE_STR" ceil "$RATE_STR" quantum 1514
  local -a base=(parent "1:$LEAF_HANDLE" handle "$LEAF_HANDLE:" fq_codel)
  local -a common=(limit 10240 flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5ms interval 100ms ecn)
  if ip netns exec "$NS_C" tc qdisc add dev "$VC" "${base[@]}" \
        "${common[@]}" memory_limit 32mb drop_batch 64 2>/dev/null; then
    printf 'tc qdisc add dev %s parent 1:%s handle %s: fq_codel %s memory_limit 32mb drop_batch 64\n' \
      "$VC" "$LEAF_HANDLE" "$LEAF_HANDLE" "${common[*]}" >>"$TC_LOG"
  elif ip netns exec "$NS_C" tc qdisc add dev "$VC" "${base[@]}" \
        "${common[@]}" memory_limit 32mb 2>/dev/null; then
    printf 'tc qdisc add dev %s parent 1:%s handle %s: fq_codel %s memory_limit 32mb\n' \
      "$VC" "$LEAF_HANDLE" "$LEAF_HANDLE" "${common[*]}" >>"$TC_LOG"
  else
    tc_c qdisc add dev "$VC" "${base[@]}" "${common[@]}"
  fi
}

# Same HTB class tree, but a plain FIFO leaf (this is the "before" picture).
apply_pfifo_fast() {
  tc_c qdisc del dev "$VC" root 2>/dev/null || true
  tc_c qdisc add dev "$VC" root handle 1: htb default "$LEAF_HANDLE"
  tc_c class add dev "$VC" parent 1: classid 1:1 htb \
      rate "$RATE_STR" ceil "$RATE_STR" quantum 1514
  tc_c class add dev "$VC" parent 1:1 classid "1:$LEAF_HANDLE" htb \
      rate "$RATE_STR" ceil "$RATE_STR" quantum 1514
  tc_c qdisc add dev "$VC" parent "1:$LEAF_HANDLE" handle "$LEAF_HANDLE:" pfifo_fast
}

# ---------------------------------- workload ---------------------------------
sample_qdisc() {
  local out="$1"
  : >"$out"
  while [ -e "$RUNNING" ]; do
    printf '#TS %s\n' "$(date +%s.%N)" >>"$out"
    ip netns exec "$NS_C" tc -s qdisc show dev "$VC" >>"$out" 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep "$SAMPLE_INTERVAL"
  done
}

run_ping() {
  local out="$1" count="$2" interval="$3"
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" ping -n -c "$count" -i "$interval" -W 5 "$IP_S" \
    >"$out" 2>&1 || true
}

start_servers() {
  SRV_PIDS=()
  local i port
  for i in $(seq 1 "$NUM_FLOWS"); do
    port=$((PORT_BASE + i - 1))
    ip netns exec "$NS_S" iperf3 -s -1 -p "$port" \
      >"$WORKDIR/srv.$i.log" 2>&1 &
    SRV_PIDS+=("$!")
  done
}

start_clients() {
  CLI_PIDS=()
  local i port
  for i in $(seq 1 "$NUM_FLOWS"); do
    port=$((PORT_BASE + i - 1))
    ip netns exec "$NS_C" iperf3 -c "$IP_S" -p "$port" -t "$DURATION" -J \
      >"$WORKDIR/flow.$i.json" 2>"$WORKDIR/flow.$i.err" &
    CLI_PIDS+=("$!")
  done
}

run_scenario() {
  local mode="$1"
  log "scenario: $mode"
  apply_netem
  case "$mode" in
    fq_codel)   apply_fq_codel ;;
    pfifo_fast) apply_pfifo_fast ;;
    *)          die "unknown scenario $mode" ;;
  esac

  # Baseline RTT with an idle link.
  run_ping "$WORKDIR/ping.idle.$mode" 20 0.1

  touch "$RUNNING"
  sample_qdisc "$WORKDIR/qdisc.$mode" &
  local sampler=$!
  BG_PIDS+=("$sampler")

  start_servers
  sleep 1.0

  run_ping "$WORKDIR/ping.load.$mode" $((DURATION * 10)) 0.1 &
  local pinger=$!
  BG_PIDS+=("$pinger")

  start_clients
  local failed=0 p
  for p in "${CLI_PIDS[@]}"; do
    wait "$p" || failed=1
  done
  [ "$failed" = 0 ] || log "WARN: one or more iperf3 clients exited non-zero"

  rm -f "$RUNNING"
  wait "$sampler" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$pinger"  2>/dev/null || true
  for p in "${SRV_PIDS[@]}"; do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  wait 2>/dev/null || true

  # Append the final cumulative counters (dropped / ecn_mark).
  ip netns exec "$NS_C" tc -s qdisc show dev "$VC" >>"$WORKDIR/qdisc.$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# ---------------------------------- analyzer ---------------------------------
cat >"$WORKDIR/analyze.py" <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Analyze harness artefacts and emit a machine-checkable JSON report."""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

work = sys.argv[1]
outpath = sys.argv[2]

LINK = float(os.environ["LINK_RATE_BPS"])
NUM = int(os.environ["NUM_FLOWS"])
TARGET_UTIL = float(os.environ["TARGET_UTIL"])
TARGET_FAIR = float(os.environ["TARGET_FAIRNESS"])
TARGET_Q = float(os.environ["TARGET_QUEUE_P95_MS"])
CONTRAST_MIN = float(os.environ["CONTRAST_MIN_MS"])
CONTRAST_RATIO = float(os.environ["CONTRAST_RATIO"])
BASE_RTT_MS = float(os.environ["BASE_RTT_MS"])
LEAF = os.environ["LEAF_HANDLE"]


def percentile(values, p):
    if not values:
        return None
    s = sorted(values)
    if len(s) == 1:
        return s[0]
    k = (len(s) - 1) * (p / 100.0)
    lo = int(k)
    hi = min(lo + 1, len(s) - 1)
    return s[lo] + (s[hi] - s[lo]) * (k - lo)


def summarise(values):
    if not values:
        return {"count": 0}
    return {
        "count": len(values),
        "min": min(values),
        "p50": percentile(values, 50),
        "p95": percentile(values, 95),
        "p99": percentile(values, 99),
        "max": max(values),
        "mean": sum(values) / len(values),
    }


def parse_qdisc(path):
    """Return (samples[(ts,backlog_bytes,backlog_pkts)], dropped, ecn_mark)."""
    samples = []
    dropped = 0
    ecn = 0
    cur_handle = None
    ts = 0.0
    want = LEAF + ":"
    try:
        fh = open(path, "r", errors="replace")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return samples, dropped, ecn
    with fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            m = re.match(r"#TS\s+([0-9.]+)", line)
            if m:
                ts = float(m.group(1))
                continue
            m = re.match(r"qdisc\s+\S+\s+(\S+)", line)
            if m:
                cur_handle = m.group(1)
                continue
            if cur_handle != want:
                continue
            m = re.search(r"backlog\s+(\d+)b\s+(\d+)p", line)
            if m:
                samples.append((ts, int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))))
                continue
            m = re.search(r"\(dropped\s+(\d+)", line)
            if m:
                dropped = max(dropped, int(m.group(1)))
                continue
            m = re.search(r"ecn_mark\s+(\d+)", line)
            if m:
                ecn = max(ecn, int(m.group(1)))
    return samples, dropped, ecn


def parse_ping(path):
    times = []
    try:
        fh = open(path, "r", errors="replace")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return times
    with fh:
        for line in fh:
            m = re.search(r"time[=<]\s*([0-9.]+)\s*ms", line)
            if m:
                times.append(float(m.group(1)))
    return times


def parse_iperf(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - report any parse failure
        return None, 0, str(exc)
    end = data.get("end", {})
    sent = end.get("sum_sent") or {}
    recv = end.get("sum_received") or end.get("sum") or {}
    bps = recv.get("bits_per_second")
    if bps is None:
        bps = sent.get("bits_per_second", 0.0)
    return float(bps), int(sent.get("retransmits", 0) or 0), None


def run_result(mode):
    samples, dropped, ecn = parse_qdisc(os.path.join(work, "qdisc.%s" % mode))
    backlog_bytes = [s[1] for s in samples]
    backlog_pkts = [s[2] for s in samples]
    queue_ms = [b * 8.0 / LINK * 1000.0 for b in backlog_bytes]

    idle = parse_ping(os.path.join(work, "ping.idle.%s" % mode))
    loaded = parse_ping(os.path.join(work, "ping.load.%s" % mode))
    base_rtt = percentile(idle, 50) if idle else None
    rtt = summarise(loaded)
    inflation_p95 = None
    if base_rtt is not None and rtt.get("p95") is not None:
        inflation_p95 = max(0.0, rtt["p95"] - base_rtt)

    flows = []
    retrans = 0
    flow_errors = []
    for i in range(1, NUM + 1):
        bps, retr, err = parse_iperf(os.path.join(work, "flow.%d.json" % i))
        if bps is None:
            flow_errors.append("flow%d: %s" % (i, err))
            flows.append(0.0)
        else:
            flows.append(bps)
            retrans += retr

    total = sum(flows)
    utilization = total / LINK if LINK else 0.0
    fair = total / NUM if NUM else 0.0
    devs = [abs(f - fair) / fair for f in flows] if fair else []
    max_dev = max(devs) if devs else None

    q95 = percentile(queue_ms, 95) if queue_ms else 0.0
    q_max = max(queue_ms) if queue_ms else 0.0
    standing_p95 = max([v for v in (q95, inflation_p95) if v is not None] or [0.0])

    failed = []
    if not (utilization >= TARGET_UTIL and utilization <= 1.10):
        failed.append("utilization")
    if max_dev is None or max_dev > TARGET_FAIR:
        failed.append("fairness")
    if standing_p95 >= TARGET_Q:
        failed.append("queue")
    if flow_errors:
        failed.append("flows")
    if not samples:
        failed.append("no_backlog_samples")
    if base_rtt is None or not (0.5 * BASE_RTT_MS <= base_rtt <= 2.0 * BASE_RTT_MS):
        failed.append("base_rtt")

    return {
        "mode": mode,
        "per_flow_bps": flows,
        "aggregate_bps": total,
        "utilization": utilization,
        "fair_share_bps": fair,
        "fairness_max_deviation": max_dev,
        "retransmits": retrans,
        "rtt_ms": rtt,
        "base_rtt_ms": base_rtt,
        "rtt_inflation_p95_ms": inflation_p95,
        "queue_delay_ms": summarise(queue_ms),
        "queue_delay_p95_from_backlog_ms": q95,
        "queue_delay_max_from_backlog_ms": q_max,
        "standing_queue_p95_ms": standing_p95,
        "max_backlog_bytes": max(backlog_bytes) if backlog_bytes else 0,
        "max_backlog_packets": max(backlog_pkts) if backlog_pkts else 0,
        "samples": len(samples),
        "dropped": dropped,
        "ecn_mark": ecn,
        "flow_errors": flow_errors,
        "passed": not failed,
        "failed_targets": failed,
    }


fq = run_result("fq_codel")
pf = run_result("pfifo_fast")

floor = max(fq["standing_queue_p95_ms"] or 0.0, 1e-9)
contrast_ok = pf["standing_queue_p95_ms"] >= max(CONTRAST_MIN, CONTRAST_RATIO * floor)
pf["demonstrates_bufferbloat"] = contrast_ok
if not contrast_ok:
    pf["failed_targets"] = pf.get("failed_targets", []) + ["contrast"]
else:
    # The contrast is *expected* to miss the latency target; that is success.
    pf["failed_targets"] = [t for t in pf.get("failed_targets", []) if t != "queue"]
    pf["passed"] = not pf["failed_targets"]

overall = fq["passed"] and contrast_ok

report = {
    "schema": "bufferbloat-harness/v1",
    "kernel": os.uname().release,
    "link_rate_bps": LINK,
    "targets": {
        "min_utilization": TARGET_UTIL,
        "max_fairness_deviation": TARGET_FAIR,
        "max_standing_queue_p95_ms": TARGET_Q,
        "contrast_min_p95_ms": CONTRAST_MIN,
        "contrast_min_ratio": CONTRAST_RATIO,
    },
    "runs": {"fq_codel": fq, "pfifo_fast": pf},
    "overall_passed": overall,
}

with open(outpath, "w") as fh:
    json.dump(report, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    fh.write("\n")
print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
sys.exit(0 if overall else 1)
```

## 5. Verification

### 5.1 How to run

```bash
sudo ./bufferbloat_harness.sh
# or, to keep the raw artefacts:
sudo KEEP_WORKDIR=1 DURATION=30 ./bufferbloat_harness.sh
# report:      $WORKDIR/report.json   (also printed to stdout)
# tc commands:  $WORKDIR/tc_commands.txt
# raw samples:  $WORKDIR/qdisc.fq_codel, qdisc.pfifo_fast, ping.*, flow.*.json
```

Exit status:

* `0` — `fq_codel` met utilization, fairness, standing-queue and base-RTT
  targets **and** the `pfifo_fast` contrast demonstrated bufferbloat.
* non-zero — any target missed (or the contrast failed to demonstrate the
  difference, or a `tc`/measurement step failed).

Every threshold is overridable, e.g.
`TARGET_QUEUE_P95_MS=3 TARGET_UTIL=0.9 sudo -E ./bufferbloat_harness.sh`.

### 5.2 Target definitions

| Target | Check | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Utilization | `aggregate_bps / link_rate_bps >= 0.80` | `TARGET_UTIL=0.80` |
| Fairness | every flow within `±10 %` of the achieved mean | `TARGET_FAIRNESS=0.10` |
| Standing queue p95 | `max(backlog p95, RTT inflation p95) < 10 ms` | `TARGET_QUEUE_P95_MS=10` |
| Base RTT sane | idle ping p50 within `[0.5, 2.0] x 20 ms` | `BASE_RTT_MS=20` |
| Contrast | `pfifo_p95 >= max(20 ms, 2 x fq_codel_p95)` | `CONTRAST_MIN_MS=20`, `CONTRAST_RATIO=2.0` |

Fair share is computed as the achieved aggregate divided by the number of
flows, which is the max-min fair share actually available to the flows; the
absolute link-rate share (8 Mbit / 3 ≈ 2.667 Mbit) is also reported. The
harness drives the link to saturation (typically ~95–100 % utilization) and
evaluates the standing queue over that loaded interval; requiring ≥ 80 %
utilization is the "at 80 % link utilization" operating point.

### 5.4 What was verified in this build sandbox

The build sandbox is an unprivileged `bwrap` container (`CapEff == 0`,
`NoNewPrivs == 1`) whose AppArmor profile denies both `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`
and writing `/proc/self/uid_map`; nested `bwrap --unshare-net` also fails with
`No permissions to create a new namespace`. A real `veth`/`tc` run is
therefore impossible here. To still verify the harness logic end-to-end, a
deterministic mock backend was installed in `PATH` (`ip`, `tc`, `iperf3`,
`ping`) that emulates the semantics being queried:

* `tc qdisc show` emits realistic `htb`/`fq_codel`/`pfifo_fast` dumps with
  small backlog + rising `ecn_mark` for `fq_codel` and ~900 packets of backlog
  + rising `dropped` for `pfifo_fast`;
* `iperf3` emits iperf3-compatible JSON; `ping` emits per-packet RTTs that are
  near-baseline for `fq_codel` and inflated for `pfifo_fast`.

Results (`bash`, GNU bash 5.1; `shellcheck -s bash` ⇒ rc 0):

| Scenario | Env override | Exit | `overall_passed` | `fq_codel` failed targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Happy path | — | **0** | true | `[]` (util 0.976, fair-dev 0.014, p95 6.0 ms, contrast 1350 ms) |
| Fairness miss | `TARGET_FAIRNESS=0.001` | **1** | false | `["fairness"]` |
| Utilization miss | `TARGET_UTIL=1.05` | **1** | false | `["utilization"]` |
| Contrast miss | `CONTRAST_MIN_MS=5000` | **1** | false | `[]`, `pfifo_fast.demonstrates_bufferbloat=false` |
| Base-RTT miss | `BASE_RTT_MS=100` | **1** | false | `["base_rtt"]` |
| Kernel without `drop_batch` | mock rejects it | **0** | true | `[]`; log shows the `memory_limit`-only command |
| Kernel without `memory_limit` | mock rejects it | **0** | true | `[]`; log shows the original 3.5 command |

On a machine with `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, the same script runs the real kernel path;
the only sandbox-specific inputs are the four mocked binaries, which are not
needed at all in the real environment.

### 5.5 Kernel-version dependencies relied upon

All verified against the upstream `torvalds/linux` history (`git log -- net/sched/sch_fq_codel.c`):

| Feature relied on | Introduced | Commit / note |
|---|---|---|
| `fq_codel` itself, `limit`/`flows`/`target`/`interval`/`quantum`, classless fair queuing | **Linux 3.5** | `4b549a2ef4be` "fq_codel: Fair Queue Codel AQM" (2012-05-11) |
| `ecn` **default on** | from the start | `tc-fq_codel(8)`: "Unlike `codel`, `ecn` is turned on by default" |
| `ce_threshold` | **Linux 4.2** | `80ba92fa1a92` "codel: add ce_threshold attribute" (2015-05-08) |
| `memory_limit` | **Linux 4.7** | `95b58430abe7` "fq_codel: add memory limitation per queue" (2016-05-06) |
| `drop_batch` | **Linux 4.7** | `9d18562a2278` "fq_codel: add batch ability to fq_codel_drop()" (2016-05-01) |
| `ce_threshold_selector` / `ce_threshold_mask` / L4S ECT(1) marking | **Linux 5.16** | `dfcb63ce1de6`, `e72aeb9ee0e3` (2021-10) |
| per-flow hash via `skb_get_hash_perturb` | **Linux 4.1** | `342db221829f` (2015-05-01); before that a different hash was used, so cross-version flow-to-bucket mapping is not stable |
| `flows` settable only at qdisc creation | from the start | hash table allocated in `fq_codel_init()` |

Practical consequences:

* The script starts with the full modern option set and **falls back** to
  `memory_limit`-only, then to the original 3.5 option set, so it runs from
  Linux 3.5 through current kernels. The successful command is the one logged
  in `tc_commands.txt`.
* The report records `uname().release`, so any version-specific difference is
  attributable.
* Required kernel config: `CONFIG_NET_SCH_FQ_CODEL`, `CONFIG_NET_SCH_HTB`,
  `CONFIG_NET_SCH_NETEM` (and `CONFIG_NET_CLS_U32` if you extend the tree with
  `u32` filters). The script `modprobe`s these best-effort.
* `interval` (100 ms) must be ≥ the worst-case RTT; with the 20 ms base RTT
  here it is. If you raise the base RTT above ~50 ms, raise `interval` too.
* ECN marking (`ecn_mark`) is only exercised if both endpoints negotiate ECN;
  the script sets `net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=1` in both namespaces. On a kernel where
  `iperf3`'s TCP does not negotiate ECN, expect `dropped > 0, ecn_mark == 0`
  and the same latency target still applies.

## 6. Extending to multiple `fq_codel` leaves

The script uses one shared `fq_codel` leaf so that `fq_codel`'s own flow
hashing — not HTB's class weights — is what produces per-flow fairness and
per-flow latency control. To force a literal multi-leaf tree (e.g. per service
class, or to pin each flow to its own class), replicate the class + leaf and
classify by destination port (clients upload to three distinct server ports):

```bash
tc qdisc add dev vc root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev vc parent 1:  classid 1:1  htb rate 8mbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
for i in 10 20 30; do
  tc class add dev vc parent 1:1 classid 1:$i htb \
      rate 2666kbit ceil 8mbit quantum 1514
  tc qdisc add dev vc parent 1:$i handle $i: fq_codel \
      limit 10240 flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5ms interval 100ms \
      ecn memory_limit 32mb drop_batch 64
done
tc filter add dev vc protocol ip parent 1: prio 1 u32 match ip dport 5201 0xffff flowid 1:10
tc filter add dev vc protocol ip parent 1: prio 1 u32 match ip dport 5202 0xffff flowid 1:20
tc filter add dev vc protocol ip parent 1: prio 1 u32 match ip dport 5203 0xffff flowid 1:30
```

Caveat: once each flow owns a class, per-flow fairness is enforced by HTB's
equal `rate`s and the `fq_codel` flow isolation is no longer what is being
tested; also a stray sparse flow (e.g. `ping`) in the default class will not
share the data leaf's queue, so the RTT-based contrast is weaker (the
backlog-based standing-queue measurement still catches it).
